Technical details:
### Bug Summary When _nx_driver_hardware_packet_send() is called with a packet setting NX_INTERFACE_CAPABILITY_PTP_TIMESTAMP, a transmit timestamp isn't captured. ### Detailed Description Packets setting NX_INTERFACE_CAPABILITY_PTP_TIMESTAMP should capture a timestamp on transmit. For STM32H5 variants with MULTI_QUEUE_FEATURE there is the following code: C if (packet_ptr -> nx_packet_interface_capability_flag & NX_INTERFACE_CAPABILITY_PTP_TIMESTAMP) { HAL_ETH_PTP_InsertTxTimestamp(&eth_handle); } However, no such code exists for variants without MULTI_QUEUE_FEATURE. issues.issue_title: [Bug]: HAL RCC VCO computation are incorrect for fractional multiplier
issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: [Bug]: HAL RCC VCO computation are incorrect for fractional multiplier
Context: repo=stm32h5xx-hal-driver, mcu_series=H5, board=None, component=None, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=medium, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=open, issue_number=31
Root cause: Hello @kasjer, Thank you for your report.
Fix: ### Bug Summary HAL and LL functions dealing with VCO use floating point numbers that don't have enough precision ### Detailed Description VCO value maximum value is 560 MHZ (560000000).
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H5, HAL, bug_report, medium, bug, internal bug tracker, rcc, VCO, MHZ, PLL, LL_RCC_CalcPLLClockFreq, FRACN

Technical details:
### Bug Summary HAL and LL functions dealing with VCO use floating point numbers that don't have enough precision ### Detailed Description VCO value maximum value is 560 MHZ (560000000). This number has 9 decimal digits value in this range requires 32 bits to represent float variables have on 6-9 decimal digits (fraction part has 23 bits) so it's clear that not all values can be represented. Lets consider function for calculation of PLL clock for P Q or R c uint32_t LL_RCC_CalcPLLClockFreq(uint32_t PLLInputFreq, uint32_t M, uint32_t N, uint32_t FRACN, uint32_t PQR) { float_t freq; freq = ((float_t)PLLInputFreq / (float_t)M) * ((float_t)N + ((float_t)FRACN / (float_t)0x2000)); freq = freq / (float_t)PQR; return (uint32_t)freq; } While formula is consistent with Datasheet calculated values may be incorrect depending on input values due to float_t being used. If for example values are as follow PLLInputFreq = 4000000 M = 1 N = 134 FRACN = 1855 PQR = 2 Returned value is 268437760 Hz When same function works on double precision numbers result is 268437744 Hz This gives 16 Hz difference. I guess double precision computation yields more accurate result. Here is version that gives same result as double precision computation using 64 bit integers c uint32_t LL_RCC_CalcPLLClockFreq(uint32_t PLLInputFreq, uint32_t M, uint32_t N, uint32_t FRACN, uint32_t PQR) { uint64_t freq = (((uint64_t)PLLInputFreq * (N * 0x2000 + FRACN)) / (M * 0x2000)) / PQR; return (uint32_t)freq; } Other places in **stm32h5xx_hal_rcc.c** also use float numbers for computation and probably also are not accurate. Same problem applies to stm32h7 devices but those do have double precision floats that could be used instead of integer computation. Computed frequency difference between current function and double precision/integer computation goes up to 30Hz ### Expected Behavior _No response_ ### Actual Behavior _No response_ ### Environment _No response_ ### Severity Minor

Key comments:
Hello @kasjer, Thank you for your report. This issue has been tracked internally. ST Internal Reference: CDM0062939

Problem: [Bug]: SPI is disabled too early
Context: repo=stm32h5xx-hal-driver, mcu_series=H5, board=NUCLEO-H563ZI, component=None, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=high, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=30
Root cause: Hello @ChST8512, Thank you for the report.
Fix: ### Bug Summary When the last (or single) byte of a data transfer has been sent, the SPI is disable too early ### Detailed Description **SPI disabled to early** When sending data via SPI, the peripheral is disabled afterwards.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H5, NUCLEO-H563ZI, HAL, bug_report, high, bug, spi, bsp, IMAGE, ATTACHED, CH1, SPI1_SCK

Technical details:
### Bug Summary When the last (or single) byte of a data transfer has been sent, the SPI is disable too early ### Detailed Description **SPI disabled to early** When sending data via SPI, the peripheral is disabled afterwards. some investigation showed that it seems to be disabled to early, while the last clock cycle is still ongoing. [IMAGE ATTACHED] Screenshot from oscilloscope shows CH1: SPI1_SCK, CH2: SPI1_MOSI. Both SPI1_SCK and SPI1_MOSI will fade their signal, instead of perfectly finishing the last bit until the clock will do its falling edge. Better to wait for a short time, e.g wait for the TXC complete flag in the SR, and then disable the SPI. The original code in **stm32h5xx_spi.c** looks like this: ~~~C static void SPI_CloseTransfer(SPI_HandleTypeDef *hspi) { uint32_t itflag = hspi->Instance->SR; __HAL_SPI_CLEAR_EOTFLAG(hspi); __HAL_SPI_CLEAR_TXTFFLAG(hspi); /* Disable SPI peripheral */ __HAL_SPI_DISABLE(hspi); ... ~~~ I suggest something similar like the following, to add a check on the TXC flag and a timeout. The code is **not** yet thoroughly tested and needs to be revised. (Of course we don't like magic numbers, and no blocking loops.) ~~~C static void SPI_CloseTransfer(SPI_HandleTypeDef *hspi) { uint32_t itflag = hspi->Instance->SR; __HAL_SPI_CLEAR_EOTFLAG(hspi); __HAL_SPI_CLEAR_TXTFFLAG(hspi); /* Disable SPI peripheral */ int32_t timeout = 1000; while ((hspi->Instance->SR & SPI_SR_TXC) == 0) if (--timeout<0) break; __HAL_SPI_DISABLE(hspi); ... ~~~ ### Expected Behavior SPI1_SCK to do all 8 cycles of the clock including the last falling edge before it is disable after a complete transfer. ### Actual Behavior SPI1_SCK does only 7 clock cycles plus an 8th rising edge. ### Environment NUCLEO-H563ZI, X-NUCLEO-PLC01A1, STM32CubeIDE V2.1.1, STM32CubeMX V6.17, STM32Cube FW_H5 V1.6.0; SPI1: 8bit, 31.25kHz, Clock to SPI 4MHz; HCLK: 250MHz ### Severity Normal

issues.issue_title: [Bug]: Raw Ethernet packet sending adds two headers leading to buffer underflow
issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: [Bug]: Raw Ethernet packet sending adds two headers leading to buffer underflow
Context: repo=stm32h5xx-hal-driver, mcu_series=H5, board=None, component=ETH, layer=Other, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=medium, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=open, issue_number=27
Root cause: Hello @ben5049, Thank you for your report.
Fix: ### Bug Summary When using any functions in NetXduo that send raw packets the STM32H5 Ethernet driver adds an extra garbage header and underflows the packet buffer.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H5, ETH, bug_report, medium, bug, hal, internal bug tracker, STM32H5, nx_link_ethernet_packet_send, nx_link_ethernet_header_add, nx_link_raw_packet_send, nx_stm32_eth_driver

Technical details:
### Bug Summary When using any functions in NetXduo that send raw packets the STM32H5 Ethernet driver adds an extra garbage header and underflows the packet buffer. ### Detailed Description When NetXduo sends a gPTP packet the following steps happen: 1. nx_link_ethernet_packet_send() is called 2. A header is added by the function nx_link_ethernet_header_add(). This is the correct header with the right destination and ethertype. 3. nx_link_ethernet_packet_send() calls nx_link_raw_packet_send() 4. nx_link_raw_packet_send() calls nx_stm32_eth_driver() with nx_ip_driver_command = NX_LINK_RAW_PACKET_SEND 5. nx_stm32_eth_driver() calls _nx_driver_packet_send() 6. _nx_driver_packet_send() prepends another header with incorrect destination and ethertype 7. The packet is sent by _nx_driver_hardware_packet_send() The resulting two headers can be seen in this image: [IMAGE ATTACHED] - In blue are the destination addresses, note that they are different and the first one is incorrect. - In red are the source addresses. - In green are the ethertypes, again the first one is invalid. To make things worse _nx_driver_packet_send() doesn't check if there is enough space to add this second header and so it underflows the packet buffer. To fix this NX_LINK_RAW_PACKET_SEND needs to be handled separately to NX_LINK_PACKET_SEND. Current: C case NX_LINK_ARP_SEND: case NX_LINK_ARP_RESPONSE_SEND: case NX_LINK_PACKET_BROADCAST: case NX_LINK_RARP_SEND: case NX_LINK_PACKET_SEND: case NX_LINK_RAW_PACKET_SEND: { /* Process packet send requests. */ _nx_driver_packet_send(driver_req_ptr); break; } Improved: C case NX_LINK_ARP_SEND: case NX_LINK_ARP_RESPONSE_SEND: case NX_LINK_PACKET_BROADCAST: case NX_LINK_RARP_SEND: case NX_LINK_PACKET_SEND: { /* Process packet send requests. */ _nx_driver_packet_send(driver_req_ptr); break; } case NX_LINK_RAW_PACKET_SEND: { /* Process raw packet send requests. */ _nx_driver_raw_packet_send(driver_req_ptr); break; } And then something like: C static VOID _nx_driver_raw_packet_send(NX_IP_DRIVER driver_req_ptr) { /* For raw packets, the Ethernet header is already attached */ NX_PACKETpacket_ptr = driver_req_ptr->nx_ip_driver_packet; UINT status; /* Determine if the packet exceeds the driver's MTU. */ if (packet_ptr->nx_packet_length > NX_DRIVER_ETHERNET_MTU) { /* Indicate an unsuccessful packet send. */ driver_req_ptr->nx_ip_driver_status = NX_DRIVER_ERROR; /* Link is not up or packet too big, simply free the packet. */ nx_packet_transmit_release(packet_ptr); return; } /* Transmit the packet through the Ethernet controller low-level access routine. */ status = _nx_driver_hardware_packet_send(packet_ptr); if (status != NX_SUCCESS) { driver_req_ptr->nx_ip_driver_status = NX_DRIVER_ERROR; nx_packet_transmit_release(packet_ptr); } else { driver_req_ptr->nx_ip_driver_status = NX_SUCCESS; } } ### Expected Behavior A packet is sent with one header ### Actual Behavior A packet is sent with two headers and memory is corrupted ### Environment TheadX, NetXduo ### Severity Major

Key comments:
Hello @ben5049, Thank you for your report. This issue has been tracked internally. ST Internal Reference: CDM0062848

Problem: [Bug]: HAL_ETH_PTP_SetTime() adds to the time instead of overwriting it
Context: repo=stm32h5xx-hal-driver, mcu_series=H5, board=None, component=ETH, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=medium, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=26
Root cause: Hello @ben5049, Thank you for your report.
Fix: ### Bug Summary TSUPDT is used instead of TSINIT to set the timestamp counter value leading to wildly fluctuating timestamps.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H5, HAL, ETH, bug_report, medium, bug, st community, TSUPDT, TSINIT, ETH_MACTSCR_TSUPDT, RM0481, nx_stm32_eth_driver

Technical details:
### Bug Summary TSUPDT is used instead of TSINIT to set the timestamp counter value leading to wildly fluctuating timestamps. ### Detailed Description On [line 1695 of stm32h5xx_hal_eth.c](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32h5xx-hal-driver/blob/38ca4af5b1004d3f9e02003ca489df7d065b75ba/Src/stm32h5xx_hal_eth.c#L1695) ETH_MACTSCR_TSUPDT is used to set the timestamp counter, however page 2934 of RM0481 says this bit is used to add or subtract from the timestamp counter instead. Based on the description of this function, and its use [elsewhere](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32-mw-netxduo/blob/79232767cef83e20573f2fbc173810f9d29c8fdb/common/drivers/ethernet/nx_stm32_eth_driver.c#L2572), this function should instead use ETH_MACTSCR_TSINIT to overwrite the timestamp counter. As it is at the moment, the current time is added to the counter every time there is a PTP sync meaning the time fluctuates wildly over a century and a half span, and the time is never close enough to use fine adjustment methods. Note: I also put this issue on the [STM Community site](https://community.st.com/t5/stm32-mcus-embedded-software/stm32h5-hal-eth-ptp-settime-adds-to-the-time-instead-of/m-p/898661/highlight/true#M75563). ### Expected Behavior The timestamp counter is set ### Actual Behavior The timestamp counter is added to ### Environment _No response_ ### Severity Normal

Hello @ben5049, Thank you for your report. This issue is already being tracked internally and will continue to be followed through the related ST Community post. Therefore, please allow us to close this GitHub issue.

Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H5, HAL, DMA, bug_report, high, bug, wontfix, internal bug tracker, i2c, MCU, STM32H523, STOPF

Technical details:
Hello, I am experiencing NACKs on the client side when I2C requests (write/read, write/write) are sent repeatedly back to back. This causes unintended behavior where the head node's source/destination addresses is always used for the entirety of the SPI transaction, making it impossible to ever reach any subsequent node in the Linked-List. I believe the user should be the one responsible for configuring their nodes before calling this function. This also applies to HAL_SPI_TransmiReceive_DMA and HAL_SPI_Receive_DMA. The line(s) I'm referring to: [https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32h5xx-hal-driver/blob/main/Src/stm32h5xx_hal_spi.c#L2539](url) [https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32h5xx-hal-driver/blob/main/Src/stm32h5xx_hal_spi.c#L2604](url) Attached is a simple example to describe the issue. Happy to share additional code if it would be helpful. To be more clear, the situation is as follows: 1. SPI initialized in slave mode, RX and TX DMA channels linked to SPI, DMA in Linked-List mode 2. Set up nodeA for BNDT=4 bytes and source address=ADDR_A 3. Set up nodeB for BNDT=4 bytes and source address=ADDR_B 4. Call SPI_Transmit_DMA(hspi, ADDR_A, 8) to transmit both buffers 5. I see 8 bytes transferred contiguously starting from ADDR_A, never goes to ADDR_B [spi_with_linked_list_test.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22179144/spi_with_linked_list_test.txt) Thank you!

Key comments:
Hello @lukewittrup, Thank you for the report. Infact, when transfers are done in LinkedList, the transfer size given to HAL_SPI_Transmit_DMA() must be the size of the first buffer of the first node. It mustn't be the size of cumulated buffers. HAL_SPI_Transmit_DMA() will start the first node and next nodes will be automatically started by DMA at the end of previous node. The size, source address and destination address of second and third transfer must be defined in configuration of second and third nodes. Hello @lukewittrup, Please, allow me to close the issue. Thank you in advance for your understanding.

The problem disappears if internal temp. channel is not used at all. **Additional context** Based on reading of the source code, the problematic place is this: https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32h5xx_hal_driver/blob/main/Src/stm32h5xx_hal_adc.c#L3519 ADC_Enable will execute the "sensor stabilization delay", which takes a considerable amount of time. Key comments:
Hello @koniarik, The ADC has been configured to perform two tasks in a 10KHz loop. Firstly, it reads channel 0 using DMA for multiple reads, and secondly, it reads the temperature sensor. This means that the same ADC is being utilized for multiple tasks and is reconfigured each time. An issue arises when the temperature sensor channel remains active, causing a delay in the stabilization process of the temperature sensor. This delay further causes the ADC to wait when it needs to read channel 0. To optimize the process, my recommendation would be to disable the temperature sensor when it is not in use. This will prevent any unnecessary delays and ensure that time is not wasted. Thank you again for your contribution. How? And frankly, is it trully the best idea?
